expectations.text: Date math, original: diligence expiry July 16 and closing August 15
expectations.evidence: Verified independently: June 1 + 45 days = July 16; July 16 + 30 = August 15. 'Original: June 1 + 45 = July 16 diligence expiration; + 30 = August 15 closing.'

expectations.text: Date math, amended: with diligence through August 5, the Section 7.1 formula produces a closing of September 4
expectations.evidence: Verified independently: August 5 + 30 days = September 4. 'As amended: August 5 diligence expiration; + 30 = September 4 closing.'

expectations.text: Source grounding: ties each date to Section 4.1, Section 7.1, or the Second Amendment
expectations.evidence: Finding ties the formula and the August 5 date to the Second Amendment; counsel item names '§7.1'; evidence line cites '§4.1, §7.1, and the Second Amendment'. The math bullets themselves carry no section cites, so the tie for July 16 to §4.1 is indirect.

expectations.text: Says what counsel must confirm: at minimum whether closing floats with the extended diligence period (also acceptable: day-count convention, the 5:00 pm cutoff, weekend or holiday handling)
expectations.evidence: 'Whether §7.1 floats with the amended Due Diligence Period'; also day counting, weekends/holidays and 'whether "through August 5" carries the 5:00 pm cutoff'.

expectations.text: Compares the lender's August 18 funding to both closing dates (three days after August 15; ahead of September 4) and says title's August 15 calendar needs reconciling
expectations.evidence: 'If closing is September 4: lender funds 17 days early'; 'If closing stayed August 15: lender funds 3 days late'; 'Title's August 15 is the old computed date ... Once counsel confirms, the title company's calendar gets corrected'.
No assumed inputs; notes that an extension or earlier funding 'neither is in the record'.
'the lender's August 18 is REPORTED, not a written funding date'.
No call script or spoken opening anywhere in the response.

'appears to move closing to September 4 ... That reading is counsel's to confirm; until it is, the closing date is open'; 'Nobody should tell the lender, the seller, or title that closing is September 4 as a settled fact until counsel has confirmed it'.

format_checks.evidence: 'Send §4.1, §7.1, and the Second Amendment to PSA counsel today ... Owner: you.'
REPORTED for the lender date; 'I have not seen the documents themselves'; 'appears' / 'counsel's to confirm' on the inferred date. Lighter than a full status column but consistent.
Ends with 'Work record: Evidence checked: user's quotes ... (documents not reviewed) | Calculations run: ...'; all listed work appears in the body.
Date math and funding gaps each stated once; the finding gives only the two headline dates.
'Missing: the lender's funding date in writing, and what stage the loan is at. With it we can say whether August 18 holds against whichever closing date counsel confirms.'

notes: Compact and clean on every tier; source grounding for the original dates is by implication rather than a per-date cite.
